name: Welcome to the New Ragnarok Reborn — Player's Guide

text.content:
You found this page tucked into the compendium cabinet like a map someone folded in a hurry. It is not lore. It is better: it is a list of things you can use.

The cast

  • Ewoklin, Prankster of the Grove — a trickster who fights with claws, spears, and a mischievous streak a mile wide. If the GM splits him, suddenly there are more of him. This is not a drill.
  • Ewoklings — his minions. Small, quick, surprisingly rude.
  • Umbrathor, the Shadow Tyrant — the reason the lanterns lean. He comes in two sizes: full nightmare, and the smaller one the deep roads remember. Bring fire.
  • Vorath, Demon Lord of Helheim — spells, legendary actions, and a throne room that hates you. Bring a plan, then bring a better one.

The places

  • Umbrathor's Shadow Cavern — the dark here is a rules lawyer. Walls, lights, and atmosphere are already built into the map; when the GM drops it in, it just works.
  • Vorath's Hellheim Throne Room — braziers, chains, and dread included at no extra charge.

The treasures

  • The Cloak of Shadows and the Amulet of the Night — real, draggable magic items with working effects. See The Treasures page, or skip straight to the good part in the party handout: @UUID[JournalEntry.LootHandoutsUmbr01.JournalEntryPage.{The Cloak of Shadows}]{The Cloak of Shadows} and @UUID[JournalEntry.LootHandoutsUmbr01.JournalEntryPage.{The Amulet of the Night}]{the Amulet of the Night}.

Everything in the packs is drag-and-drop. No importing, no re-linking, no apology.

Monsters (mostly your GM's problem)

  1. Open the New Ragnarok Reborn — NPCs compendium.
  2. Drag a creature onto the map — a token appears, and its whole sheet (attacks, spells, legendary actions, lair actions, effects) comes with it.
  3. Roll things by clicking them on the sheet. If a chat card shows a different bonus or DC than this module's guides promise, tell your GM: the module has tools for catching exactly that.

Scenes

  1. The two battlemaps live in the scenes compendium with their walls, lighting, and sounds pre-built.
  2. Drag one into the Scene Directory (or let your GM do it), then activate it. No wall-drawing, no light-fiddling — the cavern is already dark where it's supposed to be dark.

Magic items (this one's for you)

  1. Open the Treasures compendium.
  2. Drag the Cloak of Shadows or Amulet of the Night onto your character sheet's inventory. Yes, really — the item keeps its full power when it lands on a hero.
  3. Both require attunement (ask your GM, and maybe ask what else is already occupying your soul-slot).
  4. Once attuned, equip the item and toggle its effect on. The cloak turns on Stealth advantage in dim light or darkness; the amulet adds its rider to your attacks automatically while it's on.

Handouts like this one

Journals open straight from their compendium. The party handouts are marked player-readable; if a page is labelled GM's Eyes Only, do the honorable thing.

The mechanics, minus the poetry. The poetry lives with the handouts.

Cloak of Shadows

Wondrous item, rare (requires attunement)

While wearing it in dim light or darkness, you have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. The effect is a toggle: equip the cloak, switch it on when the lights drop, and watch your sneaking improve.

Amulet of the Night

Wondrous item, rare (requires attunement)

While wearing it, when you deal necrotic damage to a creature with a melee or ranged spell attack, the target takes an extra 1d6 necrotic damage. Warlocks and gish: this is a kiss from the deep roads. (The fainter copy carried by the Shadow Tyrant's weaker reflection deals only 1d4 — the crystal remembers what it used to feed.)

Both items keep working exactly as described forever — if a roll ever contradicts this page, the roll is wrong and your GM has tools to prove it.
